Riboflavin synthase is subsequently targeted by Selaginellin A and Cannabisin D, which are compounds that may modulate cellular processes involving the transporter. The presence of these intermediaries implies a possible mechanism by which Ginsenoside Rb3 could influence the activity of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be elucidated. The scores from the two paths indicate a consistent level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that the observed evidence supports a plausible biological link. However, further experimental validation is necessary to confirm the direct interaction and functional significance of this pathway.
